Germany, Italy and Japan, allied by pact since 27 September, now dominate Europe and press in the Far East, and Washington is rushing measures to defend the Western Hemisphere.

No great power is any longer fighting Germany in the west, so the United States faces a victorious Germany, Italy and Japan without an ally, and the fate of the British fleet is the most anxious question in Washington.

items.text: BOSTON—Coast artillery National Guard units were ordered today to man the harbor forts at once, a month ahead of schedule. Officers at Fort Banks said searchlight drills will run nightly, and fishing boats were warned to keep clear of the outer harbor channels after dark until further notice.

HALIFAX, N.S.—A steamer crowded with British families, among them several hundred children, docked this morning after a crossing under Canadian naval escort. Relatives from New York and New England met the ship. Canadian officials said further sailings from Irish ports are expected, and they asked American churches for blankets and winter clothing.

DES MOINES—The Navy recruiting station here reports a record week, with 212 young men from Iowa enlisting since Monday. Recruiters said quotas were doubled after word from Washington that new destroyers and cruisers need crews by spring. Applicants must be 17 to 31, and those under 21 need a parent's consent.

Wool and rubber prices rose sharply on the New York exchanges this week, as shipments formerly routed under British control were held in port pending word on Atlantic convoy arrangements. Clothing manufacturers warned that overcoat prices may advance before Christmas.
